beats.say: In nineteen sixty-nine, a government lab assistant in Gujarat started making washing powder in a small room at home.
lines: in a small room at home

beats.say: Twenty years later, India's biggest soap company had a strategy with one goal. Stop him.
This is the story of Nirma. The man who took on a giant with a bicycle, and the real girl behind the girl on the packet.
lines: and the real girl on the packet

beats.say: Karsanbhai Patel was born in nineteen forty-five, into a farming family in Patan, Gujarat. He studied chemistry, and took a job in the state government's mining and geology department.
After office hours, he mixed detergent in a ten by ten foot room at his house.
Then he did something no big company would do. He sold it door to door, on a bicycle, covering about fifteen kilometres a day.
The price? Three rupees fifty a kilo. The market leader, Surf, cost thirteen rupees.
About a quarter of the price. For families watching every rupee, that changed everything.
He needed a name. He chose his daughter's. Nirupama. At home, they called her Nirma.
Nirupama died young, in a car accident. Her father put her on every packet. The little girl in the white frock is her memory.
lines: on every packet is her memory

beats.say: So every time India hummed that Nirma jingle, it was hearing a father's tribute to his daughter.
So how did a one-man brand beat a multinational? By cutting every cost the customer didn't need.
No fancy box. No frills. Just a plain packet, and the lowest price in the shop.
And he went where the big brands didn't bother to go. Small towns, and villages.
Then came television. The twirling girl and the jingle made Nirma a household name. By the mid nineteen eighties, Nirma had overtaken Surf as India's best-selling detergent.
Hindustan Lever was not used to losing. Its answer had a name. STING. Strategy To Inhibit Nirma's Growth.
In nineteen eighty-eight, it launched Wheel. A low-priced detergent, aimed straight at Nirma's buyers.
lines: low price, aimed at Nirma's buyers

beats.say: Soon after, Procter and Gamble arrived with Ariel and Tide.
The man with the bicycle now had the world's biggest soap companies chasing him.
Nirma fought back on their turf. In nineteen ninety-two, it launched bath soaps. In about six years, it had sixteen percent of the soap market.
But the real move was quieter. Nirma started making the raw materials that go into detergent.
In two thousand seven, it bought Searles Valley Minerals in the United States, and became one of the world's seven biggest soda ash makers.
lines: Buys a US soda ash maker

beats.say: In twenty sixteen, it bought Lafarge's cement business in India for one point four billion dollars. In twenty twenty, Emami Cement, for five thousand five hundred crore rupees.
And in twenty twenty-three, seventy-five percent of Glenmark Life Sciences, a medicine ingredients maker, for five thousand six hundred and fifty-two crore rupees.
He even started a university. Nirma University, in Ahmedabad, in nineteen ninety-five.
In twenty ten, Karsanbhai Patel received the Padma Shri. In twenty twenty-four, Forbes put his fortune at about six billion dollars.
All of it started with a ten by ten room, a bicycle, and a little girl's name.
